title: Night Line Dash
premise: A neon-lit arcade survival runner where the player pilots a futuristic rail vehicle through three track lanes while dodging oncoming trains in a midnight city.
interaction_model: Single-screen, tap-or-click lane switching; left half of the screen moves left, right half moves right; tap to start and restart.
objective: Survive as long as possible and clear as many incoming trains as possible without colliding.
progression: Endless score attack progression with gradually increasing speed and denser obstacle pressure rather than distinct levels.
theme: Futuristic neon rail chase in a midnight cyber-city.
mood: Arcade, tense, sleek, energetic, and replayable.
likely_audience: players who enjoy fast reflex games
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core mechanic is a three-lane endless dodge runner.
High confidence that the game is designed for touch-first/mobile-safe play.
Moderate confidence on exact fiction: the vehicle reads as a hybrid between a car, hovercraft, and train-themed runner avatar.
High confidence that score equals cleared obstacles and that collision immediately ends the run.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a polished single-screen HTML5 canvas arcade game called "Night Line Dash" where the player pilots a bright yellow futuristic rail runner through three vertical lanes on glowing midnight tracks. The game should open on a stylish start overlay with neon sci-fi typography, a short tagline about dodging incoming trains, and a tap-to-start prompt. Once the run starts, the full screen becomes a fast endless survival challenge: the player vehicle sits near the bottom of the screen and can only swap between the left, center, and right lanes by tapping or clicking the left or right half of the screen. Incoming enemy trains spawn ahead in random lanes and rush downward toward the player; the player must dodge them by shifting lanes at the right time. Each obstacle cleared off-screen increases the score by one, while the overall game speed slowly ramps up and spawn pressure increases to create escalating difficulty. A collision should instantly trigger a dramatic game-over sequence with crash sound, particles, screen shake, a short delay, and a restart overlay showing the final cleared score. Present everything with a sleek neon-night palette, glowing rails, a faint city skyline backdrop, glassy HUD panels, readable score text, quick feedback badges like lane shift and clean dodge, and optional celebratory/crash reaction visuals. Keep the loop simple, readable, responsive, and highly replayable, emphasizing tight lane-dodge timing, mobile-friendly pointer controls, and fast restart flow over complex progression systems.
